reasoning: The disagreement stems entirely from tool failures, not security concerns. The qwen3-235b model encountered HTTP 400 errors when attempting to review 3 files (acore_mod, acore_setup, jemalloc.patch), resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 9 files and found them safe with thorough reasoning. All files contain standard AUR packaging elements: a PKGBUILD with no top-level code execution, systemd service files, helper scripts for local administration, a setup utility, and a compatibility patch. No malicious behavior, network exfiltration, or supply-chain attack patterns were identified in any file.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen3-235b model failed to review 3 files due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), causing it to return inconclusive. The deepseek model reviewed all files successfully and found them safe. This is not a genuine security disagreement but a coverage gap caused by tool failure in one model.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to review acore_mod, acore_setup, and jemalloc.patch due to API errors (HTTP 400)
Tool errors should not produce security verdicts; the system should fall back to other models' successful reviews
learnings: Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to security uncertainty' and 'inconclusive due to tool failure' - API errors should not influence the security verdict
When multiple models are used, aggregate coverage: if one model fails to review files due to errors, use successful reviews from other models to fill gaps
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for API failures to prevent coverage gaps from affecting verdicts
Tool infrastructure should track and report API failures separately from security findings to avoid conflating operational issues with security assessments
